correctness.rationale: All seven cases are proved by finite exact certificates. Explicit admissible codes attain the integer lower bounds. At lengths 1–5, deletion-output transversals give equality for the fractional LP. At lengths 6–7, nonnegative rational primal and dual certificates agree at 4 and 6; quarter-unit weighted pairwise-confusability clique covers total 15/4 and 23/4, so integer solutions have size at most 3 and 5. The verifier reconstructs every distinct shadow and validates every inequality, while a separate complete finite clique search corroborates all integer optima. No inference from finite enumeration to an unproved infinite assertion is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2012 general fractional hypergraph method applies abstractly to our constrained inputs, but its displayed RLL special case imposes endpoint zero-runs and different spacing hypotheses. Its direct general run-count covering bound is 121/15 at length six and 73/6 at seven, strictly weaker than the certified fractional optima 4 and 6. The companion paper treats unrestricted/constant-weight deletion graphs; its coding and coloring results do not determine the exact capacities of the no-11 source.

value.rationale: The classical deletion-shadow LP and graph/hypergraph matching relaxations naturally motivate determining the first finite length where they cease to be integral for the elementary Fibonacci constrained language. The exact gap at length 6 and persistence at length 7 quantify the limitation of the standard capacity relaxation and identify the need for valid weighted conflict-clique inequalities. Complete, independently reconstructible small certificates provide a benchmark for designing stronger bounds. No claim of broad asymptotic improvement is needed or made.
